_README:
Rulings that DISAGREE with what every scraped source spells, applied LAST by the builder -- after the overlay, the insert-set split and the self-naming filter, all of which are entitled to run on the source's own words first. See loadOverrides()/applyOverride() in build-parallel-vocabulary.cjs for the mechanism and why the additive overlay (checklist-parallel-overlays.json) cannot do this: its merge rule lets the SOURCE win once one exists, which is backwards for a ruling that overrides an EXISTING source spelling.

Each entry is scoped to an exact (sport, year, setKey). `drop` removes names case-insensitively even though a source stated them; `add` is the ruling's own spelling, appended only if not already present after the drop. Re-applying is idempotent.

overrides.ruling: Drew, 2026-09-25 -- the unnumbered non-auto Super Box exclusive rung is spelled "Silver Crackle Foil", matching the spelling PR #2427 folds the 2026 catalog onto. A corpus that adopts sales onto "Foilboard" (or a boilerplate-suffixed variant) would fight that fold in the 03:00Z nightly.
overrides.reason: C:/tmp/ci/csv2/2026-topps-series-1-baseball.csv (not yet committed to the repo) spells this rung "Silver Crackle Foil (Super Box exclusive)" on every base row -- the cleaner does not strip the parenthetical (a channel/box exclusivity note is normally a REAL distinction) or the word "exclusive", so the source spelling would otherwise win. The 2025 sibling products spell the analogous rung "Silver Crackle Foilboard" (Series 1/2) or "Silver Crackle Foil" (Update Series) -- see PR body for the full breakdown; only 2026 is ruled here.
